selectionCriteria: Rank commonness using current BLS2025 national occupation headcounts, cross-check actual TWC2024 Austin/Travis-area base employment; do not substitute growth rates, wages, prestige, recognition, or search popularity for frequency.

The50 are an editorial coverage set, not the mathematical50largest occupations. Prioritize wholly missing broad groups, common roles, different education/training routes, and clear roles with defensible salary inputs.
Include common hourly/transition jobs and realistic advancement routes. Managerial destinations remain explicitly separated from school-leaver entry roles.
Avoid spending multiple slots on O*NET specialties that share one BLS occupational count. BLS counts refer to occupation groups, not each O*NET subcode.

Existing health/science/engineering and arts coverage is already substantial; omitted niche specializations in those fields stay grouped while office,retail,hospitality,warehousing,safety,production,and personal-care gaps are filled.
Defer actors and musicians from salary-driven expansion until hourly/irregular-work modeling is implemented; retain them under creative fields with official links.
Grouping807remaining titles is navigation, not evidence that they are unsuitable or all rare. Common nonselected jobs remain visible under their fields.
